data.title: Midday Need to Know: Trump’s AI meeting, PayPal takeover speculation & more
data.description:
U.S. equities pushed higher Friday as yields eased and further development around the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz continued.

The blue-chip Dow was last +0.9%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +0.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite () was last +0.6%.

Now, here are 4 news stories that broke in the morning to watch out for:

Trump and Speaker Johnson to meet with top tech CEOs on AI safety: President Donald Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson  plan to host leading technology executives at the White House on Tuesday, Sept. 29, for discussions on artificial intelligence safety and potential government oversight. The meeting follows rising concerns from experts about AI's destructive potential without proper guardrails, though Trump has dismissed such warnings as a "hoax" while emphasizing the need for U.S. firms to outpace China in the AI race.

Natural gas prices fall 5.5% as pipeline leak impact proves brief: U.S. front-month Nymex natural gas futures  dropped 5.5% to $3.115/MMBtu on Friday, reversing much of Thursday's 9% surge that followed a force majeure on TC Energy's Mountaineer Xpress pipeline in West Virginia. The leak had cut firm transportation service by 1.8 Bcf/day, affecting roughly 1.5% of total U.S. Lower-48 gas supply. Analysts at Ritterbusch & Associates noted the outage appears likely to be brief, adding that Thursday's sharp price response was exacerbated by heavy speculative short positioning built up during the summer's storage cushion.

PayPal ticks up amid rumors of West Coast tech takeover interest: PayPal shares  rose 1.2% on renewed acquisition speculation after traders cited a Betaville report indicating an unnamed West Coast technology company may be evaluating an all-stock takeover of the fintech firm. The PayPal board is said to prefer an all-cash deal. The speculation follows the collapse of talks between a Stripe and Advent consortium, which had considered offering as much as $68 per share in cash but abandoned the pursuit last month after negotiations stalled over a $2 billion breakup fee.

Elevated short interest keeps squeeze risk high for crypto-linked stocks: Short-squeeze risk remains  elevated across major bitcoin-linked equities, according to S3 Partners Director of Research Leon Gross. Strategy, Strive, and Coinbase each show return correlations above 0.70 with bitcoin, while short interest hovers near 10-13% of float for Strategy and Coinbase. Bitcoin has rallied more than 50% from its lows this year but remains down year to date. S3 noted that Strive, with its smaller market capitalization of roughly $3 billion, experienced a squeeze in August when shares rose sharply alongside declining short interest, while larger names like Strategy ($65 billion market cap) and Coinbase ($53 billion) remain too large for short covering alone to drive similar moves.

data.title: Yields bite, but 'smart money' still gorging on AI - Vanda
data.description:
"Equity positioning has de-risked meaningfully this week as higher yields start to bite, but the composition is more constructive than the headline suggests," Vanda Research said in a Friday note.

Institutional investors are demonstrating notable resilience amid macroeconomic volatility stemming from a steep bond-market rout. Specifically, one-month institutional options flows stand at +$18.4B, which is roughly three times the typical flow volume seen during September, Vanda noted.

More crucially, these flows have reversed course and trended upward over the past five sessions, providing a reasonably constructive signal for risk appetite beneath the broader market de-risking.

Rather than retreating entirely, institutional capital is actively being deployed into select artificial intelligence equities. Per Vanda's options flow data, Meta Platforms is the most-bought mega-cap stock by institutions this week and is on track for its third-biggest week of institutional call buying in two years.

Over a four-session span, institutions added $603M of net call exposure to Meta . This aggressive positioning is second only to Micron Technology across the entire market, while Meta's gross call turnover has surged 243% above last week's levels.

Ultimately, Vanda said, the data indicate that macro uncertainty is not stopping risk-taking; it is simply forcing investors to be far more selective.

data.title: Cipher Digital Stock Rises as Contracted Revenue Tops $9 Billion
data.description:
Cipher Digital , a developer and operator of large-scale data centers, rose 3.43% in premarket after it agreed to extend the lease on its Barber Lake data center in Colorado City, Texas, to 20 years from 10. The deal raises total contracted revenue at the site to more than $9 billion from $3.8 billion.

Cipher amended its existing lease with Fluidstack, and an unnamed leading AI lab made a binding commitment to lease the facility for a further 10 years once that term ends, on substantially similar economics. The second term is expected to bring in about $5.2 billion of additional contracted revenue. CEO Tyler Page said the extension "reflects the enduring value of the infrastructure we're building."

The amendment also accommodates changing tenant requirements. Data halls will now be delivered in phases from the fourth quarter of 2026 through the first quarter of 2027, with rent starting as each hall comes online. Cipher will absorb the first $359.3 million of costs above the original budget, and the tenant will cover 50% of anything beyond that, repaid as additional rent over the 20-year term with a contracted return for Cipher.

data.title: Iran will make no nuclear concessions, Iranian official says
data.description:
Iran will show no flexibility over its nuclear program even if the United States accepts its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which calls for steps including the lifting of a US naval blockade on Iranian ports, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Friday.

The official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said the waterway would remain closed until “all of Iran’s conditions are met” by the United States.

Under Iran’s proposal, Tehran has offered to reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. Within seven days, hostilities would end on all fronts, including Lebanon, the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release Iran’s frozen funds and waive its oil sanctions, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said on Thursday.

The proposal follows a sharp escalation in Middle East tensions after seven months of war between Iran and the United States, with Iran-backed Houthi militias in Yemen launching missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia.

data.title: Soybean spot basis continues to firm as crushers seek supplies, corn basis steady-weaker
data.description:
Spot basis bids for soybeans firmed in the US Midwest on Friday, with basis bids improving as crushing plants continued to try to source soybean supplies, spot checks showed.

  • Spot basis for corn was steady to weaker.

  • Soybean processors in the western US Midwest are offering hefty premiums for immediate deliveries of the oilseed as persistent rains delay the early harvest, tightening supplies and forcing some plants to scale back production, according to interviews with grain merchandisers and publicly reported company data.

  • That stress on supplies is starting to show up in basis bids in the central and eastern bands of the Midwest.

  • On Friday, a processor in Morristown, Indiana, improved its spot basis bid for soybeans by 15 cents, to 40 cents a bushel over Chicago Board of Trade November (SX26) soybean futures for crop delivered by Sunday — and then the basis bid flips to 20 cents under futures for deliveries made for the rest of this fall.

  • Similarly, a soy processor in Lafayette, Indiana, improved its spot basis bid for soybeans by 15 cents to 25 cents over CBOT November futures for deliveries made by September 30. The basis bid then switches to 25 cents under futures for deliveries made starting October 1.

  • And a processor in Council Bluffs, Iowa, posted a spot basis bid of $1.00 over November futures for soybeans delivered by Monday.

  • Meanwhile, one elevator located in the Cincinnati, Ohio, area had no posted bids for soft red winter wheat on Friday.

  • CBOT November soybeans (SX26) were down 2 cents at $13.15-1/2 a bushel in midday trading on Friday, while December corn (CZ26) was down 2 cents at $5.25-1/2 a bushel.

data.title: Perplexity AI sued by startup for allegedly stealing 'wake word' technology
data.description:
By Blake Brittain

Startup DaVoice has sued Perplexity AI in California federal court for allegedly stealing trade secrets related to "wake word" technology for AI assistants.

  • The heavily redacted complaint, filed on Thursday, said that Perplexity stole DaVoice's secrets after the companies collaborated on unspecified technology "built with DaVoice’s proprietary source code, inference logic, network architecture, training approaches, training data, and know-how."

  • Spokespeople for the companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Friday.

  • DaVoice specializes in technology that allows devices to continuously listen for "wake words" to activate them.

  • The startup said that it has collaborated with companies including Volkswagen and internet-of-things company Samsara.

  • Perplexity is best known for its AI-powered search engine technology and Comet browser and AI assistant

The case is DaVoice v. Perplexity AI Inc, US District Court for the Northern District of California, No. 3:26-cv-10909.

For DaVoice: Davida Brook and Ian Crosby of Susman Godfrey

For Perplexity: attorney information not yet available

    September 25, 2026 – TheNewswire - Vancouver, BC - Baru Gold Corp (“Baru” and its subsidiary PT. Each unit comprises one common share in the capital of the Company (a “Share”) and one non-transferrable share purchase warrant (a “Warrant”). Each Warrant entitles the holder to purchase over two (2) years one (1) additional Share at an exercise price of $0.10. In connection with private placement, the Company paid aggregate cash commissions of $5,599.80 and issued 70,000 Compensation Warrants.

    The use of proceeds as previously announced remains unchanged.

    The private placement is subject to final regulatory approval, and all securities to be issued pursuant to the financing are subject to a four-month hold period under applicable Canadian securities laws. All funds are denominated in Canadian dollars.

    The securities being offered have not been, nor will they be, registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold within the United States or to, or for the account or benefit of, U.S. persons absent U.S. federal and state registration or an applicable exemption from the U.S. registration requirement.

    ABOUT SANGIHE GOLD PROJECT

    The Sangihe Gold Project (“Sangihe”) is located on the Indonesian island of Sangihe, off the northern coast of Sulawesi with a gold bearing area of approximately 25,000 ha. Sangihe has an existing National Instrument 43-101 report suitable for mining planning and production schedules for an area within the 65-ha area targeted for initial production. Within the area targeted for initial production, the National Instrument 43-101 report estimates over 200,000 oz of gold resource (Inferred: 91,000 and Indicated: 114,000), and over 3 million oz of silver resource (Inferred: 1,080,000 and Indicated: 1,930,000) as reported in the Company’s “Independent Technical Report on the Updated Mineral Resource Estimates of the Binebase and Bawone Deposits, Sangihe Project, North Sulawesi, Indonesia” (Mining Associates Pty Ltd, February 1st, 2025). Only 10% of the gold bearing area has been explored.

The Company intends to proceed to production without the benefit of first establishing mineral reserves supported by a feasibility study. The Company cautions readers that the any production decision made by the Company will not be based on a NI 43-101 feasibility study of mineral reserves that demonstrates economic and technical viability and as such, there may be involved increased uncertainty and various technological and economic risks

The remaining 30-percent interest in TMS is held by other Indonesian corporations. The term of the Sangihe CoW agreement is 30 years upon commencement of the production phase of the project. Baru has met all the requirements of the Indonesian government and has been granted its environmental permit.

data.title: European shares log weekly gains as oil prices ease, Mideast tensions linger
data.description:
Key points:
  • Konecranes tops STOXX 600 after launching buyback programme, raising targets
  • German consumer confidence slumps as energy costs bite
  • Energy shares lead sectoral declines; banks outperform

By Sudeshna Ghoshal and Purvi Agarwal

European shares snapped a three-week losing streak on Friday as oil prices retreated for most of the week, although investors remained cautious about developments in the Middle East and surging bond yields.

The pan-European STOXX 600 closed 0.4% higher on Friday, adding to the week's 0.5% advance. It was also the index's biggest weekly gain since early August. In the previous three weeks, the index had lost around 3%.

Oil prices fell again on Friday as truce hopes outweighed Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Negotiators are exploring a phased path out of war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lifting its economic blockade of Iran, sources close to the talks said this week.

"Even though the conflict in the Middle East seems like it's potentially reaching a positive phase of dialogue and agreement, there's still a lot of uncertainty because we've been here before," said Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at Capital.com.

Energy shares (.SXEP) fell 1.3% and were the biggest sectoral losers.

By contrast, oil-price-sensitive airline stocks advanced, with Ryanair and Lufthansa gaining more than 2% each. The travel and leisure index (.SXTP) rose 0.8%.

The biggest boost came from heavyweight banks (.SX7P), which were the top gainers, up 1.3%. Financial services (.SXFP) followed with a 1.1% rise.

Shares of banking major UBS rose 3.5%. A Semafor report said the bank had revived discussions to exit Switzerland.

Euro zone government bond yields were on track for their seventh consecutive weekly rise as crude prices remained near $100 a barrel and increasingly hawkish signals from central banks pushed up expectations for policy rates.

With market moves increasingly intertwined with oil prices, a retreat to below $100 a barrel earlier this week helped global equities stage a rally, though it fizzled out on Wednesday.

"Absent a shock or surprising economic or political developments, the STOXX 600 could continue to grind higher through year-end," said Paige Henderson, senior portfolio manager and head of the resilient global equity team at Allspring Global Investments.

Though Henderson warned that higher-for-longer oil prices could pressure interest-rate expectations, posing as a headwind for equities. The ECB lifted interest rates earlier this month.

Separately, German consumer sentiment weakened more sharply than expected heading into October, as rising energy prices soured households' income outlook, a survey showed.

Among individual stocks, Finland's Konecranes jumped to the top of the STOXX 600, up 7.4% after the industrial equipment maker launched a buyback programme and raised its financial targets.

Glencore PLC rose about 2% after UBS upgraded its rating on the miner's stock to "buy" from "neutral".

data.title: Treasury Bond Yields Resume Their March Higher to End the Week — 2nd Update
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani and Emese Bartha

U.S. Treasury yields rose Friday as new indications of economic resilience fuel forecasts for a prolonged cycle of interest rate increases.

The 10-year benchmark reached 5.228%, its highest intraday level since June 2007, while the 30-year rose above 5.5% for the first time in 22 years, touching 5.531%. Both eased later, but remained near record highs.

Rates may have little room to keep rising, according to Clayton Triick, head of portfolio management at Angel Oak Capital Advisors.

Rates may have little room to keep rising as the length of the Federal Reserve's hiking cycle could be overpriced, a said Clayton Triick, head of portfolio management at Angel Oak Capital Advisors.

"I think the market is peaking when it comes to hawkishness," he said. "We do not feel that effectively a 5% [federal] funds rate is necessary to bring inflation back in the direction they want...We don't think the fed funds rate will get to that level if we had to make a call today."

The rise in Treasury yields has led to investors around the world to demand higher returns on government-backed debt. The 10-year UK gilt yield reached 5.527%, before receding to just below 5.5%. The 10-year German Bund yield rose to 3.625%, then slipped to 3.592%.

The Treasury yield increases follow an upward surprise in August durable goods sales in the U.S., which were unchanged from July, but beat a Wall Street Journal consensus forecast of a small decline. The data were stronger when stripped of volatile items such as aircraft orders.

"With capital expenditure in the driver's seat of this economic cycle, orders continue to be supported by defense and AI-related infrastructure investment rather than consumer- and housing-focused manufacturing," according to a report by William Blair Equity Research.

The University of Michigan consumer confidence index declined less than expected in September to 48.1 from August's 51.7. The survey showed inflation expectations increasing.

Friday's data follow indications from earlier this week suggesting that U.S. economic growth has been fast enough to require the Fed to hike borrowing costs more than previously expected. Money markets price in a 64% probability of a second consecutive Fed hike in October, in a cycle expected to extend into next year, according to LSEG.

The rise in yields came as oil prices pared early losses and were flat, with Brent hovering around $106 a barrel.

"A pullback in oil prices helped stabilize the situation," said Patrick Munnelly, market strategist at Tickmill Group.

The dollar weakened as oil prices dropped, but remained at elevated levels. The DXY dollar index, which measures the dollar against a basket of currencies, fell 0.3% to 101.

"The U.S. dollar and Treasury yields are holding close to recent highs as expectations for further Fed tightening continue to build," said Zaheer Anwari, co-founder and CEO at The Revacy Fund. Markets' repricing of Fed rate-hike expectations continues to support the dollar and shorter-dated Treasury yields, he said.

"As long as an October hike remains the market's base case, the dollar is likely to retain an upward bias," Anwari said.

The drivers of the bonds selloff may be unlikely to dissipate soon.

"The combination of fiscal, economic, geopolitical, and supply-side inflation pressures converging has bond markets in less familiar territory," said Mike Sanders, head of fixed income at Madison Investments.

Write to Paulo Trevisani at paulo.trevisani@wsj.com and Emese Bartha at emese.bartha@wsj.com

data.title: Ankit Handa Takes Charge As CFO Of Pine Labs’ Issuing Business
data.description:
Finance leader takes charge of issuing business finance with focus on planning, profitability, governance and scalable growth

Ankit Handa has been appointed Chief Financial Officer – Issuing Business at Pine Labs, where he will lead the finance function for the company’s issuing business. His remit includes financial strategy, business planning, profitability, performance management, governance and supporting scalable growth.

Finance Leadership At Pine Labs

Handa has been with Pine Labs for nearly six years, having joined the company in November 2020 as Vice President Finance. He subsequently served as Executive Vice President Finance / IPO Readiness before taking up his current CFO role in April 2025.

In his current position, he works with business and leadership teams on financial planning and performance, with a focus on aligning finance with business priorities.

His experience at Pine Labs also includes corporate FP&A, investor reporting and IPO readiness, adding exposure to areas relevant to companies operating through periods of expansion and strategic change.

Earlier Role At OYO

Before Pine Labs, Handa spent nearly three years at OYO, where he served as Director of Financial Planning and Analysis from January 2019 to November 2020 and earlier as Senior Manager – Business Finance.

At OYO, his responsibilities included financial planning and analysis and business finance in a high-growth technology environment.

Banking Finance Experience

Handa began his career in finance roles spanning telecom and financial services. He worked at Citi as Assistant Vice President, FP&A, after spending nearly four years at SBI Card across financial planning and analysis and business finance roles.

Earlier, he was Assistant Manager – FP&A | Business Finance at Bharti Airtel, where he worked from December 2011 to August 2013.

Across these roles, Handa has built experience in financial planning, P&L management, fundraising, due diligence, investor relations, strategic finance and cost optimisation.

Focus On Business Finance

Handa’s professional background spans more than 15 years across telecom, financial services and technology-led businesses. His experience also includes building and strengthening FP&A functions, finance automation and business intelligence.

He holds an MBA in Finance from the Delhi School of Economics and a B.Com in Commerce from Delhi University.

His appointment comes as Pine Labs continues to operate across payments and financial technology, with the issuing business forming a distinct area of its operations.

data.title: Beyond scale, The Leela focuses on authentic Indian luxury
data.description:
The Brand Leadership Showcase – The Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts featured Anuraag Bhatnagar, CEO, Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts.

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

Under the theme ‘Growth Engines’, the spotlight turned to the forces that will drive India’s hospitality industry through its next phase. The Brand Leadership Showcase – The Leela Palaces, Hotels & Resorts featured Anjali Mehra, Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts.

Mehra reflected on the brand’s evolution, its enduring connection with Indian culture and the philosophy of Atithi Devo Bhava. She also highlighted the influence of Captain CP Krishnan Nair, whose vision continues to shape The Leela’s identity and approach to luxury hospitality.

“Captain CP Krishnan Nair was like a lotus in a pond for The Leela. We have ‘Atithi Devo Bhava’ at our heart at The Leela, and this philosophy is something that we have all grown up with,” said Mehra.

The Leela currently has 14 hotels across some of India’s leading destinations, with Mehra emphasising that the brand’s proposition is rooted in authenticity and Indian luxury rather than scale. She noted that international guests often perceive the traditional Indian philosophy of hospitality as an honour, adding to the distinctiveness of the experience.

“As an outsider, international guests see this as an honour to receive in India. The Leela is not about scale; we are just aspiring to create authentic experiences and build on true Indian luxury,” she highlighted.

Mehra also described The Leela as a custodian of India’s artistic and cultural heritage, with experiences forming a central part of its luxury proposition.

“We are the custodians of Indian art and culture. Luxury for us is all about experiences and bringing those experiences to life that cannot be duplicated at all,” Mehra said.

She further outlined the four pillars guiding the brand’s approach to hospitality and luxury.

“The Leela has four pillars: Grace, Nature, India and Luxury,” she explained.

The brand has also entered a new phase of growth, with The Leela becoming a listed company in 2025. Mehra highlighted the recent opening of its new flagship, Leela Coorg Sanctuary, as another milestone in the brand’s expansion.

“We became a listed company in 2025, and recently we opened our new flagship, Leela Coorg Sanctuary,” said Mehra.

Looking at the factors supporting the brand’s growth, Mehra identified access to capital and talent as significant shifts in The Leela’s journey.

“Access to capital and talent are the major shifts that have happened with The Leela for its growth over the years,” she added.

The showcase wrapped up with a compelling vision of how Indian luxury is taking centre stage globally. Anuraag Bhatnagar mapped out The Leela’s path forward, emphasising that sustainable expansion and strong owner partnerships rely on keeping heritage, design excellence, and uncompromising service standards at the very core of the brand.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. data.title: Operational excellence becomes the daily test of hospitality
data.description:
The Operational Excellence Conversations session, titled “Delivering Greatness Every Day: The New Blueprint for Hotel Operations”, was chaired by Farhat Jamal, Chairman - Travel, Tourism & Hospitality Committee, IMC Chamber of Commerce & Industry

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

Under the theme ‘Growth Engines’, the spotlight turned to the forces that will drive India’s hospitality industry through its next phase. The Operational Excellence Conversations session, titled “Delivering Greatness Every Day: The New Blueprint for Hotel Operations”, was chaired by Farhat Jamal, Chairman - Travel, Tourism & Hospitality Committee, IMC Chamber of Commerce & Industry.

The session brought together Rahul Puri, Market VP for North India, Nepal & Bhutan, Marriott International; Amitabh Rai, COO – Luxury South Asia, Accor; Anupam Dasgupta, Sr VP Operations (North India) & Head – Wellness, Leela Palaces Hotels and Resorts; Satyajeet Krishnan, SVP – Operations (North), Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL); and Gaurav Singh, COO, Chalet Hotels.

Dasgupta said wellness is moving beyond the traditional idea of indulgence towards a more holistic focus on restoration, prevention and long-term wellbeing. “The shift is from an indulgent spa experience to restoration and prevention. Today, our guests are well travelled and increasingly knowledgeable about their health. They want to stay at places where they can feel better when they leave than when they arrive. That is changing the way we look at wellness and the experiences we create for our guests,” he said.

Krishnan further noted that the company views scale not merely through the lens of adding assets, but as an opportunity to extend its culture and strengthen its people strategy across a wider footprint. “I look at scale as a great opportunity to paint your culture on a much wider canvas. Our growth strategy is in alignment with our talent strategy, because when we look at growth, we do not just look at assets but also at the growing team behind those assets,” he said.

He added that maintaining organisational culture becomes increasingly important as a company expands across markets and geographies. “Culture is the soul of an organisation, and when it scales, it should not get lost. For us, the ability to grow without diluting what IHCL and our brands stand for is about taking that culture across the geographies where we operate. Scale only creates value when the culture that built the organisation travels with it,” Krishnan said.

Singh stated Athiva was conceived around the mindset of a younger, more experience-led generation, requiring hospitality to become more flexible and responsive to individual expectations. “Athiva started as a brand for the Gen Z mindset. With that mindset, you need to create frictionless opportunities for people to engage with the brand and the experience. You have to be flexible and create an environment where your teams can deliver personalised experiences rather than simply follow a fixed template,” he said.

Singh added that Athiva’s proposition is also rooted in creating a stronger cultural connection between the brand and its customers. “With Athiva, the opportunity we have is to bring a culture that is true to our customers. It is about understanding how they think, how they travel and what they expect from an experience, and then creating a hospitality proposition that feels relevant and authentic to them,” he said.

Puri said, “Growth within our teams remains the central and most important thing for us. As we grow the business and expand our portfolio, it is equally important that we grow our people and create opportunities for our teams to develop along with the organisation.” “Operational excellence is the way we maintain quality and consistency across our hotels.

As the portfolio grows, the challenge is to ensure that the guest experience remains consistent, and operational discipline is what allows us to deliver that quality at scale.” “The algorithm of AI and the technology around it help us keep moving forward. When we bring technology and data into our operations, it gives our teams better visibility and helps us make more informed decisions. The objective is not technology for its own sake, but using it to make operations more effective.”

“We opened one hotel in Whitefield, Bengaluru, and today we have 22 hotels. That journey itself demonstrates how significantly the market has evolved and how the opportunity has grown. With that expansion comes the responsibility of maintaining the standards and brand promise that have enabled us to grow.” “Every individual or team member who joins us needs to be aligned with our brand promise. It is important that people understand not only what the brand stands for, but also what we are promising our guests. Once that understanding is clear, the team can translate the promise into the experience we deliver.”

“About 65 per cent of our associates are between 25 and 32 years old. It was interesting to see a young team member serving a younger generation, because there is a natural understanding of what that guest is looking for. That demographic connection can be a real strength for hospitality.” “We look at opportunities on a wider scale, but at the same time, we ask ourselves how we can keep things simple. Growth does not necessarily mean adding complexity. Sometimes the biggest opportunity is to simplify the way we operate, remove friction and make it easier for our teams to deliver.”

Rai addressed, “The definition of luxury has constantly been evolving, from the time when we ran hotels to what it is today, and over generations, it has been driven largely by the macro environment. Today, time for us is luxury. If we are able to give our guests time to do what they want, when they want and how they want it, I think that is what we, at our core, very strongly believe in creating in our hotels by delivering what we call frictionless experiences.

You are not putting the guest through any friction point. If I have to spend seven minutes when I just want to get to bed turning the lights off in the room, that is friction. If I order a particular dish as defined in the menu and it comes in but does not look like what was defined in the menu, that is friction. Every small thing takes away time from your guest. Our entire focus at this point is on making sure that every single person in our teams and hotels understands that concept. We have also got to give our teams time to be able to appreciate and deliver these experiences.”

As the discussion drew to a close, operations heads made a strong case for rethinking traditional hotel management. By blending smart technology with a genuinely supportive workplace culture, properties can handle higher volumes without sacrificing the personal touches and consistent quality that guests actually care about.

data.title: Hospitality’s talent challenge comes into focus
data.description:
With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

Under the theme ‘Growth Engines’, Day 2 turned the spotlight to the forces that will drive India’s hospitality industry through its next phase. The session titled, “Can Hospitality Become India's Career of Choice? Winning the Talent Battle”, brought together senior human resources and people leaders to discuss the sector’s talent priorities.

The discussion was chaired by Yateendra Sinh, Principal, YS & Associates, Sàrl, Switzerland, and brought together Vinay Jaswal, VP, HR Operations (South Asia), Marriott International; Nilesh Mitra, VP, Talent Management, ITC Hotels Limited; Amit Malik, VP - People & Culture, South Asia, Accor; Mehr Sanduja, Director - People & Culture South Asia, Radisson Hotel Group; Mielle Batliwala, VP - Human Resources, Sarovar Hotels; and Rohit Pandey, VP, Human Resources, The Leela Palaces, Hotels and Resorts.

Pandey said, “The Leela has been the aspirational brand leader in the industry when it comes to talent. I would want to explore every avenue to find the right talent, and we want to attract talent from beyond the traditional IHMs”.“This year at The Leela, we have reached out to almost 80 colleges that are not IHMs. We want to expand our talent pool and explore institutions beyond the traditional hospitality education ecosystem to find the right talent,” he added.

Malik said, “Technology signals innovation when it comes to recruitment. There is a lot of talent that hospitality industry graduates bring to the industry and contribute to the overall economy as well.” “Parents have a great influence on the career choices their wards make. This is an important factor when we look at how young talent makes decisions about their careers and the opportunities they choose,” Malik added.“We are providing leadership experiences through initiatives that allow young talent to experience work-life balance and pursue the things they want alongside their careers. We are focussed on creating experiences that make hospitality careers more relevant to the next generation,” he added.

“The industry has emotional anchors, which happen around purpose and prestige. These emotional connections are important when it comes to attracting and engaging the next generation of talent,” said Nilesh Mitra.“There was visible mentorship on the floor, and conversations with leaders were meant to inspire, not enquire. Creating those interactions and giving young talent the opportunity to engage with leaders can make a difference in how they perceive the industry,” he added.

Vinay Jaswal elaborated , “Principally, the question should change from why people are not joining us to what we are doing to make people join us. We need to look at how we can make the industry and the opportunities within it more attractive to the next generation.” “We, at Marriott, are focussed on providing experiences to the next generation.

We have interwoven career pathways across multiple segments, giving young talent the opportunity to explore different roles and build their careers within the organisation,” he explained. “We all admit that in the last decade, and especially after Covid, the hospitality industry has gone through a massive change. The expectations of talent have changed, and the industry needs to respond to those changing expectations,” Jaswal added.

Sanduja addressed, “We need to understand what talent requires from the industry. Just a monthly activity or a birthday bash is not enough to engage and retain talent. We need to look beyond routine engagement activities and understand what truly matters to our people. The focus should be on creating meaningful experiences, understanding their expectations and building an environment where they feel valued and connected to the organisation. With 20 openings planned in a year, we are looking to hire approximately 100 employees for each hotel.       ”

Batliwala elaborated, “We need to stop looking at hospitality purely through the lens of luxury. If there’s something that adds value to their learning, they will have a reason to stay with a brand for longer. When the younger generation knows that an organisation is invested in their growth and learning, they will stay longer. We are in the process of transitioning our learning system, and when we surveyed the company, we learnt that no one wants classroom training; they prefer hands-on learning. One of the biggest reasons people love working with us is that they get to work close to home. We are spread across more than 90 locations in India today, and we will need about 3,000–3,500 people over the next four years,”

As the conversation drew to a close, the panel stressed that solving the industry's staffing bottleneck requires more than just better recruitment pitches. By tackling long-standing issues around compensation, work-life balance, and continuous learning, hotel groups can build an environment where young professionals feel valued, supported, and motivated to build lifelong careers in hospitality.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. As the two-day gathering comes to a close, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have driven the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: Delhi High Court Issues Contempt Notice to Bombay Shaving Company Over Revised Advertisement; Directs Takedown
data.description:
New Delhi: The Delhi High Court has issued notice on a contempt application filed by Gillette India Limited against Visage Lines Personal Care Pvt Ltd, in proceedings concerning an advertisement alleged to be disparaging of Gillette.

The application was moved under Order XXXIX Rule 2-A read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, by Gillette alleging violation of an undertaking given before the Court by Bombay Shaving Company in relation to the original advertisement.

Gillette India submitted that despite the undertaking given by Bombay Shaving Company to take down the original advertisement, the Defendant had released a purportedly revised version which contained essentially the same offending content.

The Defendant disputed the allegations, submitting that the revised advertisement was a reworked version of the original advertisement and did not contain the allegedly offending portions or disparage the Plaintiff in law.

Importantly, upon a prima-facie viewing of the revised advertisement, the Court observed that there was “no perceptible difference in the impact” of the revised advertisement as compared to the original advertisement.

The Court has accordingly issued notice on the contempt application filed by Gillette and directed that Bombay Shaving Company shall not run the revised advertisement until the next date of hearing. The matter has been listed for 5 October 2026.

Gillette India Limited was represented by Senior Advocate Chander M. Lall, instructed by the team of Aerion Legal including Ankur Sangal, Pragya Mishra, Saumya Bajpai, Yashodhara Raina, A. Mehar and Swastik Sant.

Bombay Shaving Company was represented by Tanya Varma, Prithvi Singh, Vardaan Anand, Ruchika Yadav.

data.title: Experience takes centre stage in hotel revenue strategy
data.description:
Up next, the Revenue & Guest Experience Conversations, titled ‘Experience is the New Revenue Strategy’, brought together senior operations leaders to discuss the growing connection between guest experience and hotel performance

With the conversations of Day 1 setting the tone for what lies ahead, the BW Hotelier Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards (IHA 2026) returned for its second day at the JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity. The opening day brought together hospitality leaders, developers, investors, global brands and industry veterans, with discussions spanning growth, capital, development, leadership and the changing business of hospitality. Day 2 picked up from where those conversations left off, bringing a fresh set of voices and perspectives to the table.

Up next, the Revenue & Guest Experience Conversations, titled ‘Experience is the New Revenue Strategy’, brought together senior operations leaders to discuss the growing connection between guest experience and hotel performance.

The discussion was chaired by  Vineet Mishra, VP - Premium, Midscale & Economy, South Asia, Accor, and brought together Hemant Tenneti, Market Vice President, South & East India, Bangladesh & Sri Lanka, Marriott International; Ranjan Malakar, Sr Regional Director, Operations – South Asia, Hilton; Zubin Songadwala, VP - Operations (South & East), ITC Hotels Ltd; Vikram Berry, Sr Regional Director - Operations, South Asia, Radisson Hotel Group; and Vishvapreet Singh Cheema, President, Lemon Tree Hotels.

Vineet Mishra said the fundamentals of hospitality remain rooted in concepts that the industry has grown up with. “Hospitality and Atithi Devo Bhava are simple concepts that we have all grown up with, having heard them from our parents and experienced them through our years at IHM,” he said. However, he noted that commercial considerations have increasingly influenced the industry.

“Somewhere along the way, money came into the picture, and hospitality started taking a little bit of a back seat over the years,” Mishra said. At the same time, he stressed that strong hospitality and commercial performance need not be viewed as competing priorities. “If hospitality is done well, the question is how can your revenue grow,” he said, pointing to the need to connect guest experience with revenue generation rather than treating the two as separate objectives.

For Tenneti, consistency remains central to building guest preference. “Consistency in delivering a good stay and warm hospitality is what ultimately earns guest preference,” he said, emphasising that the guest’s experience is shaped not by a single interaction, but by the ability to consistently deliver the expected standards of stay and service.

Malakar said revenue strategy cannot be separated from the guest experience and must begin with understanding what guests need. “Revenue strategy cannot be looked at in isolation from the guest experience; the focus has to be on understanding what the guest needs,” he said. He added that people play a critical role in translating that understanding into the experience delivered on the ground.

“A very important part of revenue strategy is making sure our people understand what they need to do to keep the guest happy,” Malakar said. He also stressed the importance of giving teams the freedom to act. “We have to empower our teams to deliver the experience the guest needs, rather than creating unnecessary barriers around them,” he said, adding that the responsibility of leadership is to remove obstacles so teams can focus on guests. “Our responsibility as leaders is to remove the obstacles from our teams’ path so they can focus on what matters most, which is taking care of the guest.” According to Malakar, the right combination of empowerment and support enables teams to perform better and ultimately strengthens the overall guest experience.

Songadwala noted, “When we think and speak in our own language, we use words like ‘guest’ and ‘Atithi’, which remind us that we are the hosts. But sometimes, on the other side, we start thinking about how much we can extract from that guest. I believe that mindset has to evolve. Whether you own the property, manage it or are a partner in the ecosystem, the intent has to be the same, and the outcome has to be the same. Yes, aspirations and financial outcomes matter, but the real measure of success is whether we can put a smile on the guest’s face. If we can create that genuine experience for the guest, then we have achieved a significant part of our objective, and that is ultimately what will make the customer come back.”

Berry believes the larger revenue opportunity lies in building a relationship that extends beyond the first stay. “For me, the biggest opportunity we leave on the table from a revenue perspective is to first deliver what we have committed, so that we can earn that person’s trust and bring them into our loyalty ecosystem. Once we have done that, we can allow the guest to see what more we have to offer and create the opportunity for them to become a repeat customer.

A customer who walks in for the first time generally knows what he wants. It is during the second, third or fourth interaction, whether at the same hotel or at another hotel within the same brand, that the guest becomes more willing to listen to the suggestions and experiences that the brand may want to offer. For me, that is the most important element of revenue optimisation, because the opportunity is not simply to maximise what we earn from one stay, but to build enough trust and loyalty for that guest to keep coming back.”

Cheema shared, “Today, we have more than 130 hotels across over 80 cities, and we have also gone into Tier IV and Tier V markets, including some very remote and drive-to destinations. For us, the focus has always been on taking hospitality to where the traveller is. Whether the guest is staying with us in a large city or in a remote destination, we want to deliver a consistent experience.

But consistency does not mean that every hotel should offer an identical experience. If a guest is travelling to Sonamarg and wants to come to our hotel to celebrate or spend time with us, we have to ask ourselves how we can make that experience special for them. That is where localisation comes in. We bring in the local elements of the destination while ensuring that the guest continues to experience the consistency and familiarity of the Lemon Tree brand.”

As the session drew to a close, the speakers made a compelling case for treating hospitality as a hotel's best commercial engine. By fixing operational snags and keeping service standards sharp across the board, properties can build real emotional rapport with guests—turning everyday service into their strongest competitive edge.

The conversations will eventually give way to celebration as IHA 2026 heads into its Gala Awards evening. Bringing the two-day gathering to its culmination, BW Hotelier will recognise accomplished hoteliers and hospitality organisations across 20+ categories, acknowledging the people and businesses that have contributed to the sector’s growth and evolution.

data.title: Twilio Stock Drops After HSBC Delivers Stark Warning on Meta's Muse AI
data.description:
Twilio shares fell about 3% early Friday after HSBC cut its rating on the communications software company, citing uncertainty over how much economic value it can capture from Meta Platforms' (META) Muse AI agent.

HSBC lowered Twilio to Reduce from Hold while keeping its $211 price target. The firm said rising AI-agent activity could increase demand for calls, messages and authentication services, but higher traffic does not necessarily translate into a larger share of the resulting revenue for Twilio.

The brokerage expects Twilio's role with Muse to center mainly on connecting AI-driven calls to traditional phone networks and handling transactional or verification messages. Those services face competition from other communications providers and wholesale carriers.

HSBC also noted that Meta could choose different communications providers or establish more direct connections with carriers. That could limit the portion of Muse-related spending flowing through Twilio.

The downgrade comes as investors have recently linked Twilio to the growth of Muse, which has quickly gained attention since its launch. Reuters reported that the AI assistant had reached 2.8 million downloads within its first 12 days

The work starts with raw-material transactions. That human check is central: an answer that looks plausible still has to hold up through the close and an audit. data.title: Micron investors should get ready for a seesaw ride, analyst says
data.description:
By Britney Nguyen

The timing of an Nvidia product ramp may require a balancing act for Micron investors, as some estimated revenue shifts toward next year instead of this year

Micron's stock was down fractionally Friday morning.

As investors prepare for Micron Technology's latest quarterly results, one analyst says that more compelling opportunities lie further ahead.

Micron's (MU) revenue outlook for the November quarter should be enough to please investors, according to Susquehanna analyst Mehdi Hosseini, but it won't contain the full benefits of an Nvidia (NVDA) chip launch.

As Micron gets ready to ramp its next-generation high-bandwidth-memory technology, known as HBM4, Hosseini said investors could be due for "a teeter-totter quarter" when the company reports results on Wednesday. That refers to the balancing act that's required as estimates shift between different quarters to reflect how the Nvidia opportunity is more linked to next year.

With Nvidia finalizing its Rubin artificial-intelligence chip platform in the coming months, Hosseini said the product ramp, which is when production and shipments scale up, will likely move into April. He noted that current lead times for Nvidia's most advanced Blackwell chips are over 30 weeks, and that average selling prices for those chips are up more than 30% sequentially.

"As such, we expect the Rubin platform to be a more meaningful demand driver for HBM4 in 2027," he said. In the second half of this year, the revenue impact will be "minimal," he added.

When HBM4 does ramp, Hosseini said, average selling prices will be more than 50% higher than for the current HBM3e offering, setting Micron and other key suppliers up "to benefit handsomely."

Hosseini said he was moving "several billion dollars" of his revenue estimates from the first half of Micron's fiscal 2027, which kicked off earlier this month, into the latter end.

"All in all, we expect memory fundamentals to remain healthy," he said, adding that average selling-price trends should be better than what is currently being calculated into Wall Street's consensus.

For 2027, Hosseini is modeling for Micron's earnings per share to reach around $200, which he noted is above the consensus for $165.

Micron shares were down fractionally Friday morning but are up 277% so far this year.

-Britney Nguyen

data.title: Mpox case confirmed in northeastern Congolese city at center of Ebola outbreak
data.description:
A laboratory-confirmed case of mpox was identified in the northeastern Congolese city of Bunia, the director of a local hospital and two health officials said, raising concerns about a resurgence of the disease as the country battles its worst Ebola outbreak on record.

  • The epidemic caused by the Ebola outbreak was declared on May 15 in Ituri province, where Bunia is located, and has infected 7,890 people and killed 3,799, according to government data published on Thursday.

  • Mpox is a viral disease that causes fever and skin lesions and spreads through close physical contact.

  • Congo declared an end to mpox as a national public health emergency in April after a three-year outbreak that resulted in more than 34,000 confirmed cases nationwide. Authorities cautioned at the time that the virus had not been eradicated and could resurge.

  • The latest case involves a 21-year-old woman who was admitted to hospital on Thursday with lesions across her body consistent with mpox, hospital director Davin Ambitapio Musungufu said. She tested positive on Friday, he and two health officials told Reuters.

  • A second woman, aged 32, has been identified as a suspected mpox case and is awaiting laboratory results, Musungufu said. She and the confirmed patient have been isolated and are being cared for by a dedicated medical team.

  • Investigations are underway to trace contacts and identify the source of infection, Musungufu said.

  • Dr. Adelard Lofungola, a health official who served as deputy incident manager for Congo's mpox response, said five suspected mpox cases in Bunia were currently under investigation.

  • Health officials have reported an increase in mpox cases in several parts of the country over the past month, he said.

  • Lofungola said the Ebola outbreak's impact on Congo's health system was complicating efforts to monitor other infections.
